Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 36-year-old man with severe 4-day headache, subjective fever, generalized myalgias, diffuse pruritic blanching rash; recent travel to Thailand with mosquito exposure; friend also unwell. No photophobia, neck stiffness, focal neurologic deficits, cough, vomiting, or non-blanching rash.

Working diagnosis: Suspected mosquito-borne viral infection—most likely Dengue fever—requiring urgent face-to-face assessment and laboratory confirmation.

Supporting DDx (consistent with transcript):  
• Dengue fever – high likelihood given travel to Thailand, fever, severe headache, myalgias, blanching maculopapular rash appearing several days into illness.  
• Chikungunya virus infection – medium likelihood; similar presentation but absence of prominent arthralgia.  
• Malaria (P. falciparum) – medium likelihood; travel to endemic region and febrile headache mandate exclusion.  

Management plan:  
• Arrange urgent in-person GP assessment today for physical examination, full vitals, and blood tests (FBC, platelets, LFTs, U&Es, malaria thick/thin film or rapid test, dengue/chikungunya serology, CRP).  
• Consider referral to emergency department if no GP slot available or if concerning findings (hypotension, tachycardia, bleeding, altered consciousness) on exam.  
• Counsel patient on red-flag symptoms requiring immediate ED attendance (non-blanching rash, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, bleeding, confusion).  
• Continue antipyretics as needed; avoid NSAIDs if dengue suspected once platelet count known.  
• No antibiotics indicated at present pending evaluation.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Dengue fever – High – Travel to Thailand, mosquito exposure, fever, severe headache, myalgias, blanching rash match classic presentation.  
2. Chikungunya virus infection – Medium – Similar mosquito-borne illness with fever, headache, pruritic rash; less likely due to lack of severe arthralgia.  
3. Malaria (P. falciparum) – Medium – Febrile illness post-travel; headache and myalgias common; must be ruled out despite rash being atypical.
